definition.body: A cepstral-magnitude is the magnitude component of cepstral coefficients after inverse Fourier transform of log-magnitude spectrum, representing the envelope-like contribution of the signal in quefrency domain. Parameters: quefrency index, magnitude of cepstral coefficient, liftering window, frame length. payload.name: companding
payload.scope: People made companding to fit a signal's wide dynamic range into a fixed number of bits per sample for transmission and recording.

definition.body: Companding is a compress-expand procedure that fits a wide dynamic range signal into a fixed number of bits per sample. The compressor applies a piecewise nonlinearity to the input so that small amplitudes receive fine quantization steps and large amplitudes receive coarse ones; a uniform quantizer then maps the compressed value to a level; an expander inverts the nonlinearity at the receiver to reconstruct a linear output. Parameters: (1) the nonlinearity shape - the mu-law of ITU-T G.711 or the a-law of ITU-T G.711; (2) the number of quantization bits, 8 in the standard telephony case; (3) the sample rate. Persistence mechanism: standardized in the ITU-T G.711 and G.712 recommendations, deployed in the public switched telephone network (E1 and T1 line systems), described in DSP and telephony textbooks, and implemented in telephony hardware and software codecs. e.g.: the a-law 8-bit 3.1 kHz telephone channel of the ITU-T G.711 recommendation on E1 lines; the mu-law 8-bit channel of ITU-T G.711 on T1 lines; the G.712 32 kbit/s log-law speech coding used on the ISDN basic rate interface | not: linear 8-bit PCM (no compression, uniform steps across the full range); delta modulation (predictive coding, not compress-expand); a dynamic-range compressor for audio mixing (a loudness shaping device, not a quantizer nonlinearity) [formal: compressio expansio | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes]

payload.name: pulse-code-modulation
payload.scope: People made pulse-code-modulation to represent a continuous signal exactly enough for digital storage and transmission by sampling it at regular instants and quantizing each sample to a finite set of levels.

definition.body: Pulse-code-modulation (PCM) is a human-made procedure that represents a continuous signal in digital form by three stages. Sampling takes instantaneous values of the signal at a fixed sampling rate, typically above twice its highest frequency; quantization maps each sample to the nearest of a finite set of levels; encoding transmits the index of each level as a binary code word of a fixed number of bits. Parameters: (1) the sampling rate, 3.1 kHz in the standard telephony case; (2) the number of quantization bits per sample, 8 in the standard case; (3) the quantization law, uniform (linear) or logarithmic (the mu-law or a-law of companding). Persistence mechanism: standardized in the ITU-T G.711 recommendations, deployed in the public switched telephone network and in digital audio (the compact disc at 44.1 kHz with 16 bits), described in DSP textbooks, and implemented in every audio interface and telephony card. e.g.: the 64 kbit/s 3.1 kHz 8-bit channel of the ITU-T G.711 recommendation; the 44.1 kHz 16-bit compact disc audio track of the Red Book standard; the 8 kHz 14-bit G.703 PCM line used in digital telephone trunking | not: delta modulation (codes changes between samples, not sample values); ADPCM (adaptive step-size differential coding, a different prediction stage); a digital audio file format (a container, not the sampling-quantization procedure) [formal: modulatio impulsuum codicis | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes]

Sampling takes instantaneous values of the signal at a fixed sampling rate, typically above twice its highest frequency; quantization maps each sample to the nearest of a finite set of levels; encoding transmits the index of each level as a binary code word of a fixed number of bits. Parameters: (1) the sampling rate, 3.1 kHz in the standard telephony case; (2) the number of quantization bits per sample, 8 in the standard case; (3) the quantization law, uniform (linear) or logarithmic (the mu-law or a-law of companding). Persistence mechanism: standardized in the ITU-T G.711 recommendations, deployed in the public switched telephone network and in digital audio (the compact disc at 44.1 kHz with 16 bits), described in DSP textbooks, and implemented in every audio interface and telephony card. e.g.: the 64 kbit/s 3.1 kHz 8-bit channel of the ITU-T G.711 recommendation; the 44.1 kHz 16-bit compact disc audio track of the Red Book standard; the 8 kHz 14-bit G.703 PCM line used in digital telephone trunking | not: delta modulation (codes changes between samples, not sample values); ADPCM (adaptive step-size differential coding, a different prediction stage); a digital audio file format (a container, not the sampling-quantization procedure) [formal: modulatio impulsuum codicis | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes]
